name: TapTap Console
description: Uses the installed console-cli to discover and run TapTap Infra Console agent workflows for delivery, clusters, workloads, LightApps, migrations, inference, and on-call. No direct API calls, token storage, or bundled CLI.
whenToUse: Use for TapTap Infra Console resources. Status first; for new or unclear work, optionally use discover, help, and schema; then run exact CLI argv and read back mutations. The CLI validates commands, flags, schema, and permissions. Unsupported workflows go to Console web.

console_cli_status.description: First step before Console operations: check local CLI, version, and production login. Return safe account/permission summaries, never tokens. If missing, give the official install command on macOS/Linux; on Windows explain the script is unsupported and ask an admin for the CLI, then check again.

console_cli_login.description: Only on explicit user request, run console-cli auth login; the CLI opens OAuth and stores its session. Supply a permission level or profile, not both. If missing, give the macOS/Linux install command; on Windows ask an admin for the CLI, then check again.

console_cli_discover.description: Read the official Agent discovery. Start with overview for a new or unclear Console request; use skills when selecting a workflow. Read-only; it does not execute Console operations.

console_cli_help.description: Optionally read root help or help for a lower-case dotted command to help select a CLI command. Arbitrary flags and shell commands are not accepted.

console_cli_schema.description: Optionally use console-cli schema for a manifest-backed command's structured parameters, request body, response, and constraints; the CLI still validates execution itself.

console_cli_run.description: Run local console-cli directly with argv. The CLI validates commands, flags, schema, and permissions, including static workflows such as deploy. The plugin does not parse business arguments, preflight schema, or add context; it fixes the executable and disables shell. --token, --server-endpoint, and --web-url are rejected. Run login, upgrade, or deployment changes only on explicit user request; failures distinguish not_executed from unknown.
